subject: ClearWave trial scope — pass/fail criteria & next steps
body:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@clearwave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: ClearWave trial scope — pass/fail criteria & next steps

Hi Alice — thanks again for a productive discovery earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so ClearWave can scope the trial without ambiguity.

Summary of needs we heard:
- High-accuracy entity extraction and reply-synthesis for customer support logs (sensitive PII redaction required).
- P95 latency target for short prompts (<256 tokens) around 200–250ms under the target QPS.
- Low hallucination rate on financial facts; you called out 'false positives' on amounts as the main failure mode.
- Ability to run a head-to-head with your proprietary baseline (ClearWaveBase-v1) across a small benchmark and a long-tail prompt set.

Our proposed trial plan (three-tier):
1) Smoke (2 business days): correctness and basic throughput with 50 sample prompts.
2) Production-simulated (7 business days): 2k prompts that mirror your traffic distribution, p95 latency measured, caching exercised.
3) Long-tail validation (3 business days): 500 rare prompts + adversarial prompt set to stress hallucination.

Pass/fail (pass if ALL hold):
- Entity F1 >= 0.88 on the primary extraction schema (names, account numbers, amounts).
- Hallucination incidents <= 2% on the long-tail set (we'll mark a subset of gold facts).
- Generation quality: 90% of sampled responses rated >= 4/5 by your QA on the 100-sample blind test.
- Performance: P95 latency <= 250ms for <256-token requests when testing at your projected QPS (we'll run with a traffic replay).

Recommended model candidates to run in the trial:
- Open candidate: Llama-2-70B-chat / q4_k_mapped (quantized) with our prefix-KV caching and prompt conditioning.
- Alternate open: Falcon-40B-instruct (FP16) for lower-latency baseline.
- Fallback (if latency critical): distilled 13B variant with tuned prompts.

Why open candidates? We believe they meet your cost/latency trade-offs and can be instrumented to show direct unit economics vs ClearWaveBase-v1. If you prefer, we can also run a short baseline with a proprietary licensed model — cost impact will vary.

Attached: prompt_bundle_v1.json (sample prompt sets), benchmarks_open_vs_baseline.csv (starter metrics), sample_prompts.md.

Next steps / asks:
- Alice: confirm the primary extraction schema (I attached our tentative mapping).
- Procurement: confirm we can proceed with the 3-week trial NDA and a short MSA addendum.
- Internal (Marcus + Karthik): can you validate the quantized variant recommendations and a rough latency-cost estimate by EOD Monday?

Proposed timeline:
- July 12: kickoff + data ingest (you share the 2k prompt traffic sample via secured link).
- July 13–20: trial windows per the three tiers above.
- Jul 22: readout and go/no-go decision.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m call to walk through any item.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0199

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Alice Park <alice.park@clearwave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearWave trial scope — pass/fail criteria & next steps

Thanks for the clear plan. A few technical notes from SE / trial design perspective: 

- Latency testing: to validate P95 <= 250ms we need to confirm the target QPS envelope. Please share a 5-minute traffic sample (aggregate QPS target + percentiles). If your traffic bursts (e.g., 200–400 QPS) we'll need to run the production-simulated step on dedicated capacity.

- Model variants: for the open candidate I recommend we test both the Q4-k mapped quantization and an FP16 run. Quantized runs reduce GPU memory and cost but may degrade certain numeric extractions (amounts) — I'll flag that in the benchmark. 

- Prompt scaffolding: we'll apply a canonical prompt template that separates system-level instructions, extraction schema, and examples. See sample_prompts.md for the initial bundle. We should lock 10 canonical prompts that reflect your top intents for the smoke test.

- Data handling: PII redaction during ingestion is critical. We can ingest redacted logs (preferred) or run in a private deployment with your KMS. Let me know which.

Action items for us: Marcus will produce an initial latency/cost delta matrix for the three candidate configs by Mon 12 Jul EOD. Karthik to provide trial provisioning and any legal packaging notes.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Alice Park <alice.park@clearwave.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearWave trial scope — pass/fail criteria & next steps

Hi Soojin / Marcus — this looks good, thanks. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) For the extraction schema, we will confirm the gold labels by Thursday. We have two versions (conservative & permissive) — we'll share conservative for the trial.
2) Latency: target p95 of 250ms is our upper bound. If you can hit 180–200ms at our expected QPS that would be ideal.
3) Data: procurement prefers we run the trial in your dedicated sandbox (no customer-identifiable data leaves our environment). We can provision a redacted 2k prompt set to start.

Procurement (cc) — can you confirm the NDA timing?

I'll send the conservative label set and the traffic sample by EOD Wed.

Thanks — Alice
